title: A Ghost In Your Ear by Jamie Armitage at the Minetta Lane Theatre #ag...
transcript: It would have been embarrassing if this Audible-produced show had bad sound design. Everyone wears a set of headphones, listening to the feed of a recording booth while a voice actor records a spooky story, unknowingly inviting in the ghost that it's about. The audio we receive spatially aligns with where the actor is in relation to this microphone head, making it atmospheric and very ASMR at times. Neither the premise nor the ghost story are riveting by themselves — they seem constructed as a means to leverage the headphone gimmick, which runs thin after about a half hour. Not to undermine the genuinely impressive technical design elements here, but I wasn't very invested beyond locking in for the well-crafted suspense moments. By the end, I thought it was mostly silly, watching this guy run around caressing and whispering into this inanimate head. I appreciate what they're trying to do with this show, and I wonder how this type of sound design could be used in other genres — this one has its merits, but ultimately misses the mark for me.
